lines.trans: Chef, our newcomer stood out again.
What did you do in the kitchen again?
In the dining room the guest's tongue turned blue!
Did you ruin the soup with food coloring?
Chef, the soup turned out very delicious!

words.gloss: to turn out, to work out

lines.trans: This is how you thank me for kindness!
I gave you a chance to become a good cook.
Please, listen to me for at least a minute.
You have exactly two minutes!
Quickly pack all your things!
Chef, I did not want to offend anyone.
Leave here, you are fired from the restaurant!

lines.trans: I do not want to hear anything anymore!
Chef, our newcomer stood out again.
What did you do in the kitchen again?
In the dining room the guest's tongue turned blue!
Did you ruin the soup with food coloring?
Chef, the soup turned out very delicious!

lines.trans: This is how you thank me for kindness!
I gave you a chance to become a good cook.
Please, listen to me for at least a minute.
You have exactly two minutes!
Quickly pack all your things!
Chef, I did not want to offend anyone.

words.gram: short past pass part m sg

lines.trans: I do not want to hear anything anymore!
I do not want to hear anything anymore!

meanings.note: + accusative of the person: благодарить маму

examples.text: Всё, не благодари меня. И с Аникеевым реши.
examples.trans: That's it, don't thank me. And sort out Anikeev.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'more'.
Secondary conversational sense ('bigger') (comparative of большой) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable feminine noun meaning 'thing', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('things, belongings') (plural 'вещи') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.en: to hear out, listen attentively to
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'слушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen to', forming an aspectual pair with 'выслушивать'.

examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully.
The judge patiently heard out the witness's testimony.

examples.text: Сначала выслушай меня очень внимательно, Аркаша.
examples.trans: First listen to me very carefully, Arkasha.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'давать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'kindness', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('benevolence') (good will toward others) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий мужчина всегда оценит вашу доброту.
examples.trans: A real man will always appreciate your kindness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hall', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('living room') (regional/colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to spoil', forming an aspectual pair with 'портить'.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'dye', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.text: Повар добавил в крем синий краситель.
examples.trans: The chef added blue food coloring to the cream.
This is a natural food coloring.
This is a dye, food coloring.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: to do (something wrong), make a mess
meanings.note: Что ты натворил? = What have you done?

examples.trans: Look at what they've done here!

examples.text: Что ты натворил? — Марина, он врёт, он симулянт!
examples.trans: What have you done? — Marina, he's lying, he's a faker!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: новичкам везёт = beginners get lucky

examples.text: Говорят, что всем новичкам всегда везёт.
examples.trans: They say that all beginners always get lucky.

examples.text: Ты шутишь, шеф никогда не берёт новичков!
examples.trans: You are joking, the chef never takes novices!

meanings.en: to offend, to hurt someone's feelings
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'идеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offend, to hurt', paired with 'обижать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.
He didn't want to offend anyone.

examples.text: Извини, я не хотела обидеть. А ты что здесь делаешь?
examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you. And what are you doing here?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'again'.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.en: to distinguish oneself; (ironic) mess up, do something outrageous
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to distinguish oneself'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Our newcomer distinguished himself again today.
He distinguished himself at the culinary competition.

examples.text: Шеф, наш новичок снова сильно отличился.
examples.trans: Chef, our newcomer stood out again.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'from here'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'food', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Мы используем только безопасный пищевой краситель.
examples.trans: We use only safe food coloring.

examples.text: На кухне хранятся различные пищевые добавки.
examples.trans: Various food additives are stored in the kitchen.
Did you ruin the soup with food coloring?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('you're welcome') (answer to thanks) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('here you are') (handing something over) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

получиться.gloss: to turn out, to work out

meanings.en: to turn out, to work out
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to turn out', forming an aspectual pair with 'получаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

meanings.en: to come out of, to make
meanings.note: из тебя получится мэр = you'll make a mayor

examples.text: Классный из тебя мэр получится, Самсон.
examples.trans: You'll make a great mayor, Samson.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Secondary conversational sense ('evenly, smoothly') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'blue' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: Did you find that little blue bottle?
Did you find the vial? That little blue bottle.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to hear', forming an aspectual pair with 'услышать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to hear about') (слышать о + prepositional) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обрать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to collect', forming an aspectual pair with 'собирать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to pack') ('собрать вещи' = to pack) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги. Местные чиновники не могут собрать нужную сумму.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere. The local officials can't put together the sum they need.

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным
Secondary conversational sense ('to start (doing)') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Уходи отсюда скорее, пока шеф не увидел тебя без формы!
examples.trans: Get out of here quickly before the chef sees you without a uniform!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: нужно хотя бы поговорить = we need at least to talk
Secondary conversational sense ('although, even though (as conjunction)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: From French 'chance' (favorable turn of the dice, from Late Latin 'cadentia').

examples.text: А у меня все шансы есть. Жена, двое детей, не сидел, служил в армии.
examples.trans: And I've got every chance. A wife, two kids, no prison record, I served in the army.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
русским языком сказать = say in plain Russian
Secondary conversational sense ('tongue') (organ in the mouth) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I told you in plain Russian.
He knows the Russian language well.

examples.text: А ты не кричи на меня! Я тебе русским языком сказала.
examples.trans: Don't you yell at me! I told you in plain Russian.
